items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: And, uh, yeah, Faith to hire me for five nights out there. I went out there for the Faith to play for those five nights.

ctx.x: Wait a minute. Did the guy play for his horn or that? Mm-hmm. He didn't care, huh?

Walked out. We got the manager, the guy was giving the dance. He seemed, he claimed he's trying to trace him, but he never did. He didn't care about it. He didn't care about it. I think it's that. Mm-hmm. I'll take it. Yeah, he never did. He didn't care about it. Jim had to buy him another one. Yeah, I kept the band on the Pelican for quite a while. I stayed there about two years or something. And then, uh, meanwhile, uh, back in, uh, in the 20s, I went on the boat and played with Feed Marble out there for, uh,…
Did they have your name up? You know, did they advertise you were playing there as guest artist? No. No.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-05
items.q: And I know I had been playing with the, Fate on the jam sessions, Fate Marvel.

ctx.x: Well, he had a little bit of air on the piano. But play. Ooh, he could play some piano. And never was sober. Never was sober. He stayed right there in the same hotel with us. He wake up in the morning and get drunk. Get drunk when he eat. Twelve o'clock he get drunk. Go to work he's drunk. Come from work he's drunk. But play. Never was late on the job. And never went to sleep. Never went to sleep. But he'd be drunk. Played everything you put in front of him and what you don't put in front of him he played. He was…

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: He asked Fate to bring me out there. One night. I went out there. Stayed out there. I stayed out there. Played out there with him until he got ready to make the trip and leave.

ctx.x: Where was that? No, it was in Baton Rouge. Oh. No, it was in Baton Rouge.

Then I stayed with Toody Harris about a year. Eight months a year. I got a telegram that my wife fixed to be operated on on a Saturday. And I got the telegram that Friday evening. And that's when I left that Friday evening. Come here. And uh... That Monday I went to work at the humming board. No, I played at the entertainers. I played at the entertainers for about six, eight months. And then we left there and... I went to the humming board. And that's where I sent for Guy Kelly, trumpet player. Sent for him. And…
I didn't think I wanted to go. I was doing alright there by the hummingbird. But anyway...
